themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violations have spiked 967% this week (4 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks), suggesting a sudden change in park usage or enforcement patterns that warrants investigation into what's driving the surge.
evidence: 4 park rule violation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike, z-score: 7.49)
Converges with CB budget request for park reconstruction/upgrades, indicating ongoing park infrastructure concerns
High z-score (7.49) indicates statistically rare event
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept. about what triggered the spike—new enforcement detail, seasonal activity, or specific park incidents?
Walk Domino Park or McCarren to observe current conditions and speak with users about rule violations

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints jumped 620% this week (9 complaints vs. 1.2 weekly average), indicating rapid deterioration in sanitation services or a specific localized failure in waste collection.
evidence: 9 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (620% spike, z-score: 5.24)
Complements broader sanitation concern: Dirty Condition ranks 8th in all 311 complaints (588 over 90 days)
Suggests either route reassignment, staffing shortage, or equipment failure in specific blocks
reporting_angles: Map the 9 complaints to identify if complaints cluster in specific neighborhoods (Greenpoint vs. Williamsburg) or streets
Contact Sanitation Dept. about recent route changes, staffing, or equipment issues in CD 301

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Tree/Branch Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints surged 567% this week (5 complaints vs. 0.8 weekly average), a sudden uptick that may signal storm damage, deferred maintenance, or seasonal growth requiring urgent Parks/DOT attention.
evidence: 5 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (567% spike, z-score: 5.13)
Converges with CB budget request for park and amenity upgrades, signaling maintenance backlog
Poses safety risk if branches overhang streets/sidewalks; may indicate deferred tree trimming
reporting_angles: Check Parks Dept. tree maintenance schedule—when was last canopy management work done in CD 301?
Walk neighborhood streets to identify hazardous branches; photograph and cross-reference with complaint locations

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints exploded 1100% this week (3 complaints vs. 0.2 weekly average), suggesting either enforcement action targeting street vendors or a sudden influx of unlicensed/problematic vendors.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Williamsburg/Greenpoint has active street vending; spike may reflect enforcement push or resident backlash
Low baseline (0.2 avg) means even small number constitutes major statistical anomaly
reporting_angles: Interview Dept. of Health about vendor enforcement operations in Greenpoint/Williamsburg this week
Talk to street vendors and residents about recent complaints—unlicensed operators? sanitation issues? parking?

themes_detail.label: Root/Sewer Damage Emerges
themes_detail.summary: Root and sewer-related complaints spiked 208% two weeks ago (5 complaints vs. 1.6 weekly average), a sustained infrastructure problem suggesting underground damage that may worsen without intervention.
evidence: 5 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (208% spike, z-score: 6.97)
Converges with CB budget request for DEP capital improvements—suggests systemic infrastructure deficit
Root damage can cascade; early detection enables preventive maintenance vs. emergency repairs
reporting_angles: Request DEP data on sewer backups and root intrusions in CD 301; compare to city-wide rates
Interview residents with damaged sidewalks/foundations about timeline and repair costs; establish if city liability cases pending
